newsitem.title: USA: CSCE May coffee soars to new high on GCA data.
newsitem.headline: CSCE May coffee soars to new high on GCA data.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures vaulted to fresh life-of-contract highs in early dealings Wednesday as speculators bought heavily after a monthly report showed a much lower-than-expected rise in consumer coffee stocks, traders said.

At 0946 EDT, spot May futures were up 20.10 cents at 212.50 cents a lb, traded from a new contract high of 213.00 to 203.00. Second-month July was 14.35 higher at 189.00, while the remaining months were up 6.00 cents.

The market gapped more than 10.00 cents higher at the opening this morning after Green Coffee Association of New York reported late Tuesday that supplies of green coffee stored in U.S. warehouses rose in March by 111,000 60-kg bags to 1,657,000 bags,

Most analysts had forecast an increase of between 250,000 and 300,000 bags, with some operators looking for a build of up to 700,000 bags, after Latin America shipped heavily over the last several weeks to take advantage of higher futures prices.
"It's on the green coffee numbers," said Refco analysts Ann Prendergast. "The implication is that the influx of exports coming in were absorbed by the market."
News a strike by stevedores in at the key Barzilian port of Santos is set to spread nationally at midnight Thursday for 48 hours fueled bullish sentiment, traders said.

Stevedores at Santos began an indefinite strike Tuesday to protest steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) using its own workers to load and unload vessels at its private terminal at the port.

Technically, after flying through 202 and 205 resistance and triggering buy stops, traders said May's next upside objective would be near 220 cents. ((-- Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk, 212 859 1640))
